Rashi on Shabbat 142a:10:1.hebrew: ומאי דוחקיה כו' - דאיצטריך למימר "לא שנו אלא שהטמאה למעלה"? לשבקי כדקס"ד דעתך, בין שטמאה למעלה בין שטמאה למטה, ולוקמי בצריך למקומו:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:10:1.english: And what impelled [him], etc. - That he needed to say, "They only taught [this] when the impure [teruma] is on top"? Let him leave it as we originally thought: whether the impure [teruma] is on top or whether the impure [teruma] is on the bottom, and establish it [as referring to a case] where he needs its place.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:11:1.hebrew: אלא לצורך גופו - שצריך לכר לשכב עליו שם ולא לסלקו, לפיכך לא התירו לו ליטלו עם המעות אלא מנערו במקומו. אבל צריך למקום הכר, מטלטל הכל ביחד:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:11:1.english: Only for the purpose of [the cushion] itself - That he needs the cushion to lie upon it there and not to remove it; therefore, they did not permit him to take it with the coins, rather he shakes it in its place. However, [if] he needs the place of the cushion, he may move everything together.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:11:2.hebrew: ומדסיפא כו' רישא נמי לצורך גופו - הלכך, אי הוה טהורה למעלה, לא הוי שרי ליה לטלטולי טמאה, כדקתני גבי מעות: מנערו ונופלות, ומטלטל היתרא לחודיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:11:2.english: And from [the fact] that the latter clause, etc., the first clause, too, is for the purpose of [utilizing the basket] itself - Therefore, if the ritually pure [terumah] were on top, he would not be permitted to move the ritually impure [terumah], just as it is taught regarding coins: he shakes [the cushion] and they fall off, and he moves the permitted [item] alone.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:12:1.hebrew: הא קמתקן - שמביאה לידי היתר, ונגזר ביה אטו תיקון שע"י מלאכה:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:12:1.english: Isn't he rendering [it] fit - For he brings it to a state of permissibility, and [the Sages] should decree regarding it on account of fixing [performed] through [forbidden] labor.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:13:1.hebrew: כר"א דאמר תרומה - הואיל וניתנה להעלות אחת שירצה, בעינא מחתא — כאילו מונחת לבדה ואינה מעורבת. הלכך, לא קמתקן מידי:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:13:1.english: In accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, who said: Teruma - Since it is permitted to lift out whichever one [measure] he wishes, it is [considered] resting in its pure state — as if it is placed by itself and is not mixed [with the rest]. Therefore, he is not fixing anything.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:14:1.hebrew: מדמעת - זה שנפרד משם, ואוסר צ"ט של חולין כאילו היא תרומה ודאי:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:14:1.english: Renders [it] a prohibited mixture - This [se'a] that separated from there, and [it] prohibits ninety-nine [se'a] of non-sacred produce as though it were definite teruma.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:15:1.hebrew: וחכ"א אין המדומע מדמע - חולין אחרים, אלא לפי חשבון התרומה שבמדומע. כגון: אם תחילתו נדמע ס' של חולין ע"י סאה תרומה, וחזרה סאה ממנו ונפלה לתוך אחרים — לא חשבינן תרומה אלא ס' שבסאה זו, ומדמע עד צ"ט שכנגדו, ואם יש חולין יותר מק' כנגדו, עולה:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:15:1.english: And the Sages say: That which is meduma does not render [other things] meduma - [i.e.,] other chullin, except according to the proportion of the teruma that is in the meduma [mixture]. For example: if initially sixty [se'ah] of chullin were rendered meduma by one se'ah of teruma, and one se'ah from it then fell into other [chullin], we only count as teruma the [one-]sixtieth [part] that is in this se'ah; and it renders [the new mixture] meduma up to ninety-nine [times that amount] corresponding to it, and if there is chullin more than a hundred [times that amount] corresponding to it, [the teruma] is nullified.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:16:1.hebrew: אימר דשמעת ליה - לר"א, דאמר תרומה כמאן דמחתא בעינא:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:16:1.english: Say that you heard it - [Referring to] Rabbi Eliezer, who says [that] terumah is as though it is lying [there] intact.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:16:2.english: Stringently - To render it a [prohibited] mixture like definite terumah.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:16:3.english: To [rule] leniently - That one who lifts it out on Shabbat should not be like one who repairs [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:16:4.hebrew: מי אמר - הא ודאי מתקן הוא. ע"כ:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:16:4.english: Did he say [so]? - For he is certainly fixing [the produce]. Thus far.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:17:1.hebrew: הוא דאמר - רבי יהודה דמתני' כרבי שמעון, דאמר לקולא נמי כמאן דמחתא בעינא דמיא:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:17:1.english: He stated - Rabbi Yehuda of our Mishnah [stated his ruling] in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who says that even toward leniency, it is regarded as though it were lying intact.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:17:2.english: Into one hundred - And [the se'a of teruma] is fit to be lifted out, and the non-sacred produce will become permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:17:3.hebrew: עד שנפלה אחרת - ועכשיו אין בה חולין כדי להעלותה באחד וק':
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:17:3.english: Until another [se'a] fell - And now it does not have [enough] non-sacred produce to nullify it in one hundred and one.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:17:4.hebrew: ר"ש מתיר - קס"ד משום דס"ל ליה קמייתא כמאן דמחתא בעינא דמיא, ונמצאת אחרונה זו נופלת בתוך ק' של חולין:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:17:4.english: Rabbi Shimon permits [it] - We initially assumed [that this is] because he holds [that] the first [se'ah] is as though it is resting intact, and [consequently] this last [se'ah] is found to be falling into one hundred [se'ah] of non-sacred produce.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:18:1.hebrew: בטל בק' - והוו להו כולהו חולין, ומיהו כיון דצריך להעלותה, ע"כ המעלה מתקנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:18:1.english: Was nullified in one hundred - And they all become non-sacred produce [chullin]; however, since one must lift it out, perforce the one who lifts [it] out renders [the mixture] fit [for consumption].

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:19:1.hebrew: נותן עיניו - במדומע בצד זה להעלותו לתרומה, ואוכל בצד אחר. הלכך, הואיל ובלא העלאה מתחיל ואוכל, אין תיקון בהעלאתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:19:1.english: He casts his eyes - on the meduma [mixture] on this side to lift it up as terumah, and eats on another side. Therefore, since he begins and eats [even] without lifting [it] up, there is no [act of] rendering [it] fit in lifting it up.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:1:1.hebrew: אתי לאתויי - וטעמא לאו משום טלטול הוא, דאפילו לאוחזו בידו והתינוק מהלך ברגליו אסר ליה רבא, דילמא נפיל ואתי לאתויי. וכיון דלאו סכנת נפש היא, לא שרו ביה טלטול:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:1:1.english: [His father] will come to bring [it] - And the reason is not because of moving [muktzeh], for even holding [the child] by his hand while the child walks on his [own] feet Rava prohibited, lest [the dinar] fall and [he] come to bring [it]. And since it is not [a case of] danger to life, they did not permit moving [it] in this case.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:2:1.hebrew: תניא כוותיה דרבא - דכי נקט לה עליון, כמאן דאפקא תחתון גופיה דמי, ומיחייב:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:2:1.english: It was taught in accordance with Rava - For when the upper one [who is being carried] holds it, it is as though the lower one [who is carrying him] himself took it out, and he is liable.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:2:2.hebrew: וסנדליו וטבעותיו בידו - בקומצו, שלא כדרך מלבוש:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:2:2.english: And his sandals and his rings in his hand - In his fist, not in the manner of wearing.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:3:1.english: One who carries out a person with his garments on him - Dressed in them.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:3:2.hebrew: וטבעותיו בידיו - באצבעותיו, מדלא תנא בידו כדנקט רישא:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:3:2.english: And his rings on his hands - [Meaning] on his fingers, since it did not teach "in his hand" as the first clause stated.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:3:3.hebrew: פטור - דבגדיו בטלי לגביה, ועליו הוא פטור כרבי נתן:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:3:3.english: [He is] exempt - For his garments are subordinate to him, and for [carrying] him he is exempt, in accordance with [the opinion of] Rabbi Natan.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:3:4.hebrew: ואילו הוציאן כמות שהן - שהיה אותו עליון אחוז בהן ולא מלובש, חייב הנושא, והיינו כרבא:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:3:4.english: Whereas if he carried them out as they are - [Meaning] that the one [being carried] above was holding onto them and not wearing [them], the carrier is liable, and this is in accordance with Rava.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:4:1.english: The basket should be a base - and it itself should become prohibited.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:4:2.hebrew: מליאה פירות - דעיקר נעשית בסיס לפירות, הלכך אבן מיטלטלת אגב כלי ופירות שהוא מותר:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:4:2.english: Full of fruit - For [the basket] was primarily made a base for fruit; therefore, the stone may be moved along with the vessel and the fruit, which is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:4:3.hebrew: ונינקטינהו בידים - ילקטם מעל הארץ בידיו, ויחזירה לכלכלה ויטלטלם, ולמה התירו אבן לטלטל אגב כלי ופירות:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:4:3.english: And let him take them in [his] hands - He should gather them from the ground with his hands, return them to the basket, and carry them; and why did they permit a stone to be moved along with a vessel and fruit?

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:4:4.hebrew: בפירות המיטנפין - בפירות מבושלין ורכין מאד, כגון תאנים ותותים וענבים, שאם ישליכם לארץ יטנפו:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:4:4.english: With fruits that become soiled - [That is,] with very ripe and soft fruits, such as figs, mulberries, and grapes, which, if he throws them to the ground, will become soiled.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:5:1.hebrew: ולנערינהו נעורי - עד שיסתלקו הפירות מן האבן לתוך הכלכלה לצדדין, וישליך האבן לבדה בנעורתה:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:5:1.english: And let him shake them - Until the produce moves away from the stone to the sides inside the basket, and he casts out the stone by itself by shaking it.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:5:2.english: Broken - Whose side or bottom was broken.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:6:1.hebrew: וטמאה למעלה - והוא צריך לטהורה, ואינו יכול ליטול הטמאה בידים לפי שהיא מוקצה. לפיכך יטלטל הכל עד השלחן, וישליך הכל עליו, ויטול הטהורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:6:1.english: And [the] impure [teruma is] on top - And he needs the pure [teruma], and cannot take the impure [teruma] in [his] hands because it is muktzeh; therefore, he may carry everything to the table, cast everything onto it, and take the pure [teruma].

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:7:1.english: Let him throw them - Onto the ground, all of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:7:2.english: And let him take them - [Let him take] the pure [fruit] by hand and return it to the basket.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:9:1.hebrew: לצורך גופו - שצריך לטהורה לגופה, לאוכלה. הלכך, אי לאו דטהורה למטה, לא שרו ליה לטלטולי לטמאה, אלא שקיל לטהורה וממטי לה לשלחן:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:9:1.english: For the purpose of [the object] itself - [Meaning] that he needs the pure [terumah] for itself, to eat it. Therefore, were it not that the pure [terumah] is on the bottom, they do not permit him to move the impure [terumah]; rather, he takes the pure [terumah] and brings it to the table.

Rashi on Shabbat 142a:9:2.hebrew: ברייתא לצורך מקומו - שצריך למקום הכלי, וע"כ כולו הוא צריך לסלקו משם, ושרו ליה רבנן לטלטל האי אטו האי:
Rashi on Shabbat 142a:9:2.english: The baraita [refers to a case] for the purpose of its place - Because he needs the place of the vessel, and therefore he needs to remove all of it from there, and the Rabbis permitted him to move this [impure teruma] on account of that [pure teruma].

Tosafot on Shabbat 142a:14:1.hebrew: שנפלה לפחות מק' חולין - מכאן משמע דתרומה עולה באחד ומאה עם האיסור. ורש"י לא פירש כן בפרק גיד הנשה (חולין דף צט:) גבי "כל איסורין שבתורה במאה", דלפירו' שיטתו לא אתי' מסקנא הכי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 142a:14:1.english: That fell into less than a hundred [se'ah of] non-sacred produce - From here it is implied that terumah is nullified in one hundred and one [parts] including the forbidden [item]. However, Rashi did not explain it this way in the chapter [entitled] Gid Hanasheh (Chullin 99b) regarding [the rule that] "all forbidden things in the Torah [are nullified] in a hundred [parts]," for according to the explanation of his approach, the conclusion does not come out like this.

Tosafot on Shabbat 142a:4:1.hebrew: ונשדיינהו לפירי ונשדייה לאבן - ואם תאמר: גבי קטן נמי נשדייה לאבן מידו, ואמאי שרי לטלטולי עם האבן? וי"ל: אם ישליכו מידו, יצעק התינוק ויבכה. וא"ת: מ"ש דלא שרינן לטלטל תינוק אלא כשיש לו גיעגועין — תיבטל אבן אגב תינוק, כמו שהיא בטלה אגב כלכלה מלאה פירות? וי"ל: דאינו צריך כל כך טלטול התינוק. וא"ת: אפילו אין הכלכלה מלאה פירות, תיבטל האבן אגבה, כי היכי דבטלי בפ"ב דביצה (דף כא:) שיורי הכוס אגב הכוס, אי לאו דאיסורי הנאה נינהו? וי"ל: שאני שיורי דגריעי יותר מדאי ובטלו טפי; וכן צ"ל מתוך שמעתא גופה דביצה, כמו שפירשתי לעיל בסוף כירה (שבת דף מז. בד"ה הוה):
Tosafot on Shabbat 142a:4:1.english: "And let him throw the fruit and throw the stone" - And if you ask: Regarding a child as well, let him throw the stone from [the child's] hand, and why is it permitted to carry [him] with the stone? One can say: If he throws it from his hand, the infant will scream and cry. And if you ask: What is the difference that we only permit carrying the infant when he has longing [for his parent]? Let the stone be nullified relative to the infant, just as it is nullified relative to a basket full of fruit! One can say: Carrying the infant is not so necessary [when he has no longing]. And if you ask: Even if the basket is not full of fruit, let the stone be nullified relative to it, just as in the second chapter of Beitzah (21b) the remnants of the cup are nullified relative to the cup, were it not that they are forbidden for benefit? One can say: Remnants [of a cup] are different, because they are extremely insignificant and are nullified more readily; and so must one say from the sugya of Beitzah itself, as I explained above at the end of [the chapter] Kirah (Shabbat 47a, s.v. Havah).

Tosafot on Shabbat 142a:4:2.hebrew: ונשדינהו לפירי ונשדייה לאבן כו' - וא"ת: מכל מקום נינקטינהו לפירי בידים ויניח האבן בכלכלה! והא אמרינן לקמן: "לא שנו אלא שטהורה למטה וטמאה למעלה, אבל טהורה למעלה וטמאה למטה — שקיל לה לטהורה ושביק לה לטמאה". והיינו על כרחך בידיו, דאי זריק לה בכלי — א"כ גם בטמאה למעלה יכול לזורקה בכלי! אלא שמע מינה דשקיל לה בידיו; וא"כ, הכי נמי לשקלינהו לפירי בידיו! וי"ל, דמיירי שפי הכלכלה צר הוא ואינו יכול להכניס שם ידיו. אי נמי י"ל, דההיא דלקמן מיירי בתרומה שהיא בכלים קטנים בתוך הקופה, שאין דרך להניח טמאה וטהורה ביחד אלא בכלים — זה בפני עצמו וזה בפ"ע, ולהכי מצי שקיל לטהורה שהיא למעלה בידיו; אבל כלכלה דהכא — אין כאן כלים, ולא מצי נקיט להו בידיו פן יפול לארץ. והשתא לא צריכנא לשינויא קמא דפירות המיטנפין, דהא כיון דאבן עצמה הוי דופן לכלכלה, אפ' הוי שדי לפירות ולאבן והדר שקיל לפירי ושבק לאבן — לא הוי ליה במאי לאנחינהו, כיון שהכלכלה פחותה שהאבן נעשה לה דופן. והא דלא קאמר "אלא" — לפי שלא הוזכר אמורא לעיל. א"נ, השתא יש להעמיד נמי בפירות המיטנפין, דאל"כ נוכל להשליך הסל בקרקע ולהוליך בכלכלה מעט מעט כמה שתוכל להחזיק עד מקום הפחת. מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 142a:4:2.english: And let him throw the fruit and throw the stone, etc. - And if you say: Nevertheless, let him take the fruit in his hands and leave the stone in the basket! For we say below [in the Gemara]: "They only taught [that one may not move the basket] when the pure [terumah] is on the bottom and the impure is on top; but if the pure is on top and the impure is on the bottom, he takes the pure and leaves the impure." And this is perforce [taking it] in his hands, for if he were pouring it out with the vessel, if so, even when the impure is on top he could pour it out with the vessel! Rather, learn from this that he takes it in his hands; and if so, here too, let him take the fruit in his hands! And one can say that [here] it is dealing with [a case] where the mouth of the basket is narrow and he cannot insert his hands there. Alternatively, one can say that that [case] below is dealing with terumah that is in small vessels inside the basket, for it is not the practice to place impure and pure [terumah] together, rather in vessels — this one by itself and that one by itself — and therefore he is able to take the pure [terumah] that is on top in his hands; however, [in the case of] the basket here, there are no vessels here, and he cannot take [the fruits] in his hands lest they fall to the ground. And now [according to the Gemara's next answer], we do not need the first answer of "fruits that become soiled"; for since the stone itself is a wall for the basket, even if he were to throw out the fruit and the stone and then take the fruit and leave the stone, he would have nothing in which to place them, since the basket is breached, as the stone is made a wall for it. And the reason [the Gemara] does not say "rather" [ela] is because no Amora was mentioned above [for the first answer]. Alternatively, even now it can also be established as [referring to] fruits that become soiled, for if not so, we could dump the basket onto the ground and carry in the basket little by little, as much as it can hold up to the place of the breach. [From] my teacher.

Tosafot on Shabbat 142a:4:3.hebrew: הכא נמי בפירות המיטנפין - וא"ת: אכתי יטלם בידו ויניחם בתוך כלי אחר, או על גבי טבלא, או ע"ג סודר, כדמוכח בסמוך גבי תרומה דאמר רב חסדא: "לא שנו אלא שטהורה למטה וטמאה למעלה, אבל טהורה למעלה וטמאה למטה — שקיל לטהורה ושביק הטמאה", ואע"ג דמוקמינן נמי בפירות המיטנפין! וי"ל דהתם מיירי כגון שטהורה מונחת בסלים קטנים בפני עצמה, וכן הטמאה, ואותם סלים מונחים בתוך כלי אחד גדול, והיו סלים של טהורה למעלה מסלים של טמאה, דיכול ליקח סלי טהורה ולהניחם ע"ג קרקע; אבל אם מונחת זו על גב זו בלא שום כלי, כי הכא שהפירות מונחים ביחד, בהא ודאי לא אמר "שביק לה לטמאה ושקיל לה לטהורה". מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 142a:4:3.english: Here, too, [it is referring] to fruits that become soiled - And if you will say: Still, let him take them in his hand and place them inside another vessel, or on top of a board, or on top of a cloth — as is proven immediately below regarding terumah, where Rav Ḥisda said: "They only taught [this] when the pure [terumah] is below and the impure [terumah] is above; however, [when] the pure [terumah] is above and the impure [terumah] is below, he takes the pure [terumah] and leaves the impure [terumah]" — even though we also establish [that case] as referring to fruits that become soiled! And one can answer: There it is speaking of a case where the pure [terumah] is placed in small baskets by itself, and likewise the impure [terumah], and those baskets are placed inside one large vessel, and the baskets of pure [terumah] were above the baskets of impure [terumah], so that he can take the baskets of pure [terumah] and place them on top of the ground. However, if one is placed directly on top of the other without any vessel, like here where the fruits are lying together, in that [case] he certainly did not say "he leaves the impure and takes the pure." [From our Rabbi.]
